vo: This is Hotsauce, an open source office suite for small teams. It runs on your own server. Every morning starts on Today: your meetings, your tasks, and the to-dos your meetings left behind.
Docs are plain Markdown files, kept in Git. Write in a clean editor and link docs with two square brackets. Every save is a version, so you can step back through history and see who changed what.
Meetings takes the notes for you, and no bot joins your call. After the call, your rough notes and the transcript become clean notes, with decisions and action items.
Ask a question across every past meeting, and the answer points back to where it came from. Hotsauce also writes a brief for your AI agents, and they can read and write everything here, through MCP.
Action items land in Tasks. Type one in plain words, with a date and a project. Or just ramble for a few seconds, and Hotsauce sorts it into a clean list.
Notes hold the small stuff that isn't a doc. Color them, pin them, or turn them into checklists.
Clips replaces the meeting you didn't need. Record your screen and talk it through. Whoever watches gets a transcript and a summary.
Dictate turns talking into clean text. Hold a key on your Mac and speak into any app, or leave a voice note from your phone.
There's more on the table: whiteboards your team draws on live, a people directory, files, forms, booking links, and Briefcast, a morning briefing you can play like a podcast.
Hotsauce is free and open source, and it deploys to Cloudflare in minutes. Get it at hotsauce dot work.
